technical_eligibility_rule.interpretation: Technical operation only; not an efficiency or promotion gate

budget_estimate.kind: Planning estimate of API list-price equivalents, not a billed or guaranteed maximum
budget_estimate.limitations: Unfamiliar work can exceed historical spend; no hard total-turn token cap. Actual invoices remain unavailable.

limitations: Offline target coverage is an author-scope proxy, not semantic completeness or coding correctness.
No new native model usage, task success, token saving, latency benefit or billed saving exists until an explicitly approved formal execution.
The upstream repositories and intentionally injected defects are controlled workloads; size and source-snapshot coverage are disclosed, not described as representative production work.
Provider and operating-system caches cannot be equivalently reset; order balancing does not establish identical caching.
Native JSONL does not reveal actual billing, underlying inference-call counts, actual filesystem reads or provider CPU/memory.
Native-reported zero cache writes may be a parser default; possible-write sensitivity bounds are scenarios, not confidence intervals.
Budget approval is an estimated API-equivalent allowance, not a guaranteed spend ceiling; Codex exec exposes no hard total-turn token cap here.
All automatic-selection abstentions and failed or interrupted attempts remain in primary intent-to-treat results; originals are never retried.
Offline B/C/V1 order is balanced across tasks and reversed on repeat two; preparation timings remain local component observations, not native task latency benefits.
V1 is an offline previous-policy comparator only; formal model configurations remain A bare, B known-path source and C selective v2 source.

Technical eligibility requires repeated automatic preloads on at least half of tasks and complete declared scope on at least three quarters of known-source-preparable tasks; it does not establish efficiency or default promotion.
Parent CPU includes preparation, sampler and treatment-audit work, excludes child CPU and is not combined with sampled child CPU as an exact total.

Waited preparation-child CPU is a separate OS cumulative-counter difference around setup/preparation only; it excludes later audit/native/grading and still-running or unwaited children. No preparation peak RSS is inferred.

All native arms receive the same pinned TypeScript compiler on PATH. Upstream full development suites/dependencies are not installed; focused native checks and external behavioral grading are distinct from upstream full-suite validation.
